title: The exchange-defined projection traces are the normalized splitting traces
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an arbitrary scheme $S$ with $\ell$ invertible, and a projective-line presentation $p$ [def-sp-tower-p1-adjunction-data]. Let $d$ be its canonical map data and $h$ the etale-origin comparisons including the shifted Tate line [lem-sp-tower-p1-etale-origin-comparisons]. For any normalized splitting data $k$ with kernel scalar normalization [def-sp-tower-p1-kernel-scalar-data], the two traces $\operatorname{projectionTrace}$ defined from inverse proper exchange and the pullback of $p$'s trace [def-sp-tower-p1-triangle-words] are equal to the corresponding splitting traces of $k$: $\operatorname{projectionTrace}(h,a)=\operatorname{trace}(k,a)$ for $a=\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}$. This is an equality in the actual ordinary derived tower category, not just at finite evaluations.

source.place: Reduction of the triangle identities; Levels; standing-setting restriction

proof.text: Transpose the two ordinary coefficient comparisons and evaluate their scalar-unit normalizations. The maps agree on sections. For the line comparisons apply the same argument to the finite tensor generators a tensor z; equality of compatible families is equality of tower maps. Localize and commute the fixed shifts to identify k's shifted-line comparisons with p.line2Iso and p.line1Iso.

source.place: Reduction of the triangle identities; Levels; standing-setting restriction

proof.text: Substitute these equalities in the trace_base_change equations supplied by kernel scalar normalization. Precompose by the inverse shifted-line map and the inverse exchange mate on the shifted Tate object. Cancel inverse pairs. The two Boolean cases are exactly projectionTrace1 and projectionTrace2.
